title: CBRN Ropes Rescue Course
description: U.S. Marines with Chemical, Biological, Radiological, and Nuclear Defense Platoon, Headquarters Battalion, 3d Marine Division, rehearse rope rescue training during the culminating event of a rope rescue technician certification course at Marine Corps Air Station Futenma, Okinawa, Japan, March 23, 2023. The course, taught by U.S. Air Force firefighters, prepares Marines to respond to disaster situations and builds interoperability between joint forces for crisis response operations. (U.S. Marine Corps Video by Lance Cpl. Anna C. Geier)

transcript.text: The course we're completing today is
the rope rescue technician course . And
the key events that they had to do were
some individual events like self rescue ,
self ascension as well as building
what's called a mechanical advantage
system which is used to lift and haul
whenever they are doing rescue
operations ,
say we're operating here in Japan . And
there's a situation where individuals
are trapped in a cave or somebody who
was just doing some recreational
repelling . These marines are now
trained and capable to go and conduct
rescue operations to save lives . Prime
example , being a few years ago , there
was a situation in Thailand where some
individuals had to be rescued from a
cave . There was a joint effort in that
where multiple rope rescue teams came
in , conducted rescue operations at the
time . Seaborn Marines were not the
credential to do that . So now they are
capable of doing that and they're now a
vital asset to Third Marine Division ,
right .
